statistic: For each window (one satellite, one cutoff) and lead, the root mean square of the 3D position error against the truth over the 24 hours that end at the lead, on the truth's 300 s grid (a day counts when the truth covers 90 % of it). The median and the 95th percentile (linear interpolation) of each column are taken over the lead's windows where that column has a figure: a lead's windows are those where AP was scored, AP's column is over all of them, the numerical propagator's over those of them where it was scored too (with its own windows where the two differ), and each other theory's as stated below. xp is SGP4-XP, our clean-room build in the same module as AP (THEORY SGP4XP), fitted to the same arc by the same fit call and flown in the module's own GCRF output. xpUssf is the Space Force's SGP4-XP (propagator/sgp4-xp 0.2.1, its library the unmodified Sgp4Prop 9.1.1.0 XP build), fitted to the same arc by that module's own fitter, which searches two-line-element digits with every evaluation running the library, and flown by its propagate in its own GCRF output. sgp4 is SGP4 fitted to the same arc by analysis/gp-error-model (its own SGP4 in improved mode, B* fitted) and flown by propagator/sgp4 (AFSPC mode), its TEME output turned to GCRF by foundation/frames, the path its fit uses. Each is null until it has a row on every window of the row; a window where its fit or flight failed counts as flown. Its median and 95th percentile are taken over the lead's windows where it was scored (windows); failed counts the lead's windows where its fit or flight failed. From sdn-ap 0.6.15 the two medium Earth orbit rows of navigation satellites (GN and Galileo), and from sdn-ap 0.6.19 the geostationary, inclined geosynchronous and commercial geostationary rows, fit AP with $PCF FORCES.ECOM2 on fits of 72 h or more; from sdn-ap 0.6.26 a 24 h fit carries the terms of its 72 h fit where above drag or drag sigma >= 1; from sdn-ap 0.6.20 every row's AP fit states $PCF FORCES.SOLID_TIDES IERS 2010. within100mOfFfm counts, at the 120 hour lead and over the windows where AP and the numerical propagator both have a figure, the windows where AP's error is less than 100 m above the numerical propagator's (AP better than it counts as met); share is met over windows. apFfmRank is Spearman's rank correlation of AP's and the numerical propagator's errors over the lead's windows where both have a figure. Columns by build: ap and xp come from sdn-ap 0.7.4 (modules d557f9e2d5f7, wasm e9900159be5c), xpUssf from propagator/sgp4-xp 0.2.1, sgp4 from analysis/gp-error-model + propagator/sgp4 + foundation/frames. Over the table's 4,526 window-arcs, ap scored 4,426, failed 0; xp scored 4,422, failed 0.
ffmSelection: Each row's numerical propagator is its fullest stored FFM setting, named in the row's configuration sentence and not chosen on the outcome: on the laser geodetic spheres the full setting with ocean tides and Earth radiation pressure, else the full setting (degree and order 70, solid tides, relativity, RK78 at 1e-10, or with drag at 1e-13 where every armed window has a 1e-13 row and no window is refitted after a burn).
windows: The table holds 2,823 windows (one satellite and one cutoff each), cutoffs from 2013-02-11 to 2026-10-26; the second pass (the windows whose fit arc or 7-day forecast touches March to May 2026) is in for Near 700 km (198 windows), Medium Earth orbit (495 windows), Medium Earth orbit, Galileo (suite) (30 windows), and its 495 windows of the other rows are not in this table (a regime's second pass is in this table where its numerical rows are all in the store).

rows.fitData: the truth's states over the 24 h before the cutoff, one every 300 s (GCRF)
rows.apForces: Gravity to degree 70 in the zonal terms and 31 in the tesseral terms; the solid Earth tide (IERS 2010); atmospheric drag by NRLMSISE-00 driven by the space weather known at the cutoff; fitted for the mean elements, the drag coefficient and the radiation coefficient, with the module's stated priors.

ffm.configuration: Earth gravity to degree and order 70; atmospheric drag by NRLMSISE-00 driven by the space weather known at the cutoff (GFZ observed F10.7 and Ap, then the NOAA SWPC forecast issued before it); solar radiation pressure on a sphere; the Sun and Moon; solid Earth tides; general relativity (IERS 2010); integrated by RK78 at a tolerance of 1e-10 with steps up to 120 s; fitted by batch least squares (analysis/estimation) for the initial state, the drag area to mass and the radiation area to mass. Two flights of this same fit that differ only in the integrator's step sequence part by up to 0.9 m at 24 h, 2.8 m at 72 h and 8.4 m at 168 h (40, 33 and 38 windows).
